title: US minus European ozone increment slopes were negative over full publication spans but uncertain in two period tests
abstract: We directly tested a regional difference left open by an earlier campaign result. We used 62 invertebrate papers in a 2024 public data release. Each paper had equal weight. The US minus European slope of experimental ozone concentration increments was -64.77 ppb per publication decade, with a 95 percent interval of -99.35 to -30.19. Setting and insect-order adjustment gave -35.25, with interval -63.73 to -6.78. Separate tests through 2004 and after 2004 had corrected intervals that included zero. Restriction to the common publication-year range also gave an interval that included zero. Thus the full-span difference did not receive clear support in the period or common-year checks. This is an exposure-design result, not a biological response or climate effect. Selected studies, mixed taxa, imputed concentrations, unequal time coverage and shared research programmes limit inference. We supply code, source hashes, aggregate results and independent arithmetic checks.

display.caption: US minus European publication-year slopes for experimental ozone concentration increments. Period intervals use two-test correction. Other intervals are ordinary 95 percent intervals.
